LESSON: GENERAL ETIQUETTE

Grade: PP1
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Sadachar
Topic 6.1: General Etiquette

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on General Etiquette. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you greet your learner should be able to: digital parents/guardians/elders/friends?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups
2. appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GENERAL ETIQUETTE
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
General Etiquette helps you succeed in HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: GENERAL ETIQUETTE
Study General Etiquette like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “General Etiquette” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to General Etiquette in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what General Etiquette is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “General Etiquette” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to General Etiquette in your own words. (skill: appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach General Etiquette to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all.
4. Make one local Kenya example of General Etiquette from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for General Etiquette: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study General Etiquette?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you greet your learner should be able to: digital parents/guardians/elders/friends?
2. How do you greet the priest at greetings used at places of the different forms of the place of worship?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what General Etiquette means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate appropriate • Learner practices and role greetings to show respect for play greetings in pairs or different ages groups.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of greetings for love and respect to all.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
